title: 3D-MoE - 3D stacked near-DRAM architecture for MoE LLM with hybrid parallelism
problem: Mixture of Experts (MoE) language models require processing massive expert networks and face severe bandwidth bottlenecks when transferring data between memory and compute. Traditional flat architectures cannot efficiently scale MoE systems.
motivation: 3D stacked memory with near-DRAM compute can dramatically reduce data movement by placing expert computation adjacent to data, enabling efficient MoE scaling through hybrid parallelism strategies.
method: 3D-MoE physically stacks memory and compute layers together, placing an LLM's expert networks directly next to DRAM instead of keeping them far apart. It distributes both the data and the experts across these stacked layers—different layers handle different experts while different data flows through others. This keeps data physically close to where computation happens, eliminating the slow bandwidth bottleneck that normally occurs when experts need to access distant memory.
key_novelty: The core idea is using 3D stacking to place memory and compute next to each other, then splitting both experts and data across the layers so information stays close to processors.
contributions: 3D-stacked near-DRAM architecture for MoE LLM acceleration
Hybrid parallelism methodology for distributed MoE execution
limitations: 3D stacking technology faces significant manufacturing challenges and cost constraints, limiting near-term practical deployment feasibility.
